transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Seabright Head of Search), Daniel Ortega (Seabright Eng Mgr), Sofia Ruiz (Seabright ML Eng)
Link shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/seabright-intro (shared during call)

Summary:
Short hosted API demo showing embeddings + reranking flow, tradeoffs for using Redwood hosted endpoints vs bringing your own vector DB, and next steps for a pilot. Security questions (SOC2, SAML, KMS) surfaced and Redwood promised security brief.

00:00:03 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, super excited — quick roll call?
00:00:08 Priya Kapoor: Hi, Priya here, good morning.
00:00:09 Daniel Ortega: Daniel.
00:00:10 Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, hi.
00:00:12 Liam O'Connor: Liam from Redwood, happy to run through the rerank bits.

00:01:05 Maya Chen: Quick agenda — we'll demo hosted embeddings endpoint, show a simple bi-encoder retrieval then a rerank cross-encoder call, then walk the Console and Optimize suggestions, and finish with security/Q&A. Any additions?
00:01:17 Priya Kapoor: That sounds great; we're most interested in precision at top-5, and latency around 100-200ms for reranker stage if possible.

00:03:30 Liam O'Connor: Ok so first live demo — hitting the hosted embeddings endpoint. We send a batch of documents, Redwood returns 1536-d vectors (note: actual dim depends on model), store them in your vector store. We show the python snippet:
  - from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
  - emb = EmbeddingsClient(api_key=...)
  - vecs = emb.create(texts)

00:04:12 Sofia Ruiz: Quick Q — do you recommend we store vectors in our OpenSearch or use Redwood's managed vector index?
00:04:20 Maya Chen: Good question. Both supported. Managed index gives you less ops, native similarity search, and automatic TTL/caching; self-hosted (OpenSearch/FAISS) gives more control and sometimes cheaper at scale. For pilot we usually recommend hosted index so we can control consistency and we can demo reranking without setup.
00:04:51 Daniel Ortega: Any limits on top_k or vector cardinality?
00:05:03 Liam O'Connor: No hard limit for top_k but practical limits for latency. Typical pattern: top_k 100 for recall, then rerank top_10 with cross-encoder. If you try to rerank 1000 candidates you'll see cost/latency jump.

00:08:40 Maya Chen: Now switching to reranker demo. We call the /rerank endpoint with the query + list of candidate docs (we show JSON). Backend uses a cross-encoder style model, scores candidates and returns sorted results.
00:09:05 Priya Kapoor: Is the reranker model a separate model? Do you offer multiple sizes?
00:09:15 Liam O'Connor: Yes separate. We have small/medium/large families — small gives lower latency but may underperform on nuanced queries. Optimize will give suggestions for which family based on your eval set.

00:11:30 Sofia Ruiz: What's the KV cache behaviour? We saw references to KV cache in docs but want to know if it helps repeated prefix queries.
00:11:45 Liam O'Connor: The runtime maintains K-V cache for autoregressive models primarily; for reranker it's less relevant. For chat/generation requests it speeds repeated prefixes. In embedding/rerank pipelines caching can help if you store intermediate results at the application layer — Redwood's Console has a cache hit rate view.

00:14:20 Daniel Ortega: Security — we need SOC 2 type II, SSO/SAML, KMS integration and audit logs. Also data residency in EU.
00:14:32 Maya Chen: We support SOC 2, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS for Private deployments; hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys for enterprise accounts and we have EU regions—I'll attach the security brief.
00:15:05 Priya Kapoor: Do you do per-customer model isolation? We're concerned about noisy neighbors.
00:15:12 Liam O'Connor: For hosted we provide tenant isolation in our control plane and can offer Dedicated pools for higher isolation guarantees and predictable throughput.

00:18:00 Maya Chen: Let's walk the Console — here's the per-route latency chart, token breakdown, and rerank cost-per-call. You can pin model versions and we have canary rollouts.
00:18:30 Sofia Ruiz: Can we visualize embedding drift across model updates?
00:18:40 Liam O'Connor: Yes, Console has an embeddings drift dashboard in Optimize — it compares centroid shifts and recall on holdout queries. It can also suggest quantization profiles if you want cost reductions.

00:22:12 Daniel Ortega: How do you recommend we evaluate reranker quality? We currently look at MRR and precision@5.
00:22:22 Liam O'Connor: Good — we suggest precision@k plus normalized discounted cumulative gain (nDCG) for graded relevance. Redwood's eval harness can compute these from your labeled set and tie regression alerts to the prompt set.

00:26:40 Priya Kapoor: Cost question — can you ballpark per-100k queries for our expected traffic?
00:26:50 Maya Chen: We gave a rough example: bi-encoder embedding + vector search is X tokens/call (cheap), reranker is heavier because it's cross-encoder per candidate. For top-10 rerank with medium model, expect roughly 3–5x the cost of retrieval call. We'll send a more exact worksheet with your projected RPS.

00:31:55 Sofia Ruiz: For the pilot we'd like to test two approaches: 1) Redwood embeddings + hosted index + Redwood rerank, 2) Redwood embeddings stored in our OpenSearch + in-house rerank. How quickly can we spin both?
00:32:10 Maya Chen: We can spin the hosted flow in a day, the hybrid will take a bit longer depending on your infra. POC kickoff can include sending a small pipeline recipe and a checklist for keys/ingest.

00:36:00 Liam O'Connor: Demo of a live query — you can see the initial recall list then rerank sorts it. Note: transcription may show model names weird — we said cross encoder but transcript reads "cross 'en coder'" [laughs].

00:39:20 Daniel Ortega: Any think around latency SLOs? We need 95th percentile under 250ms for rerank in our SLA.
00:39:32 Liam O'Connor: For medium reranker model on dedicated capacity we can hit that at moderate RPS; hosted depends on concurrency and region, but Dedicated is where we guarantee percentiles. We'll include SLO numbers in the SLA doc.

00:44:10 Priya Kapoor: A tangent — for semantic search we often tune embedding dim and distance metric; do you support cosine vs L2?
00:44:22 Liam O'Connor: Yes; Console lets you pick similarity metric and the hosted index supports both. We also provide quantization profiles for lower mem use with slight impact to recall.

00:48:05 Maya Chen: Ok recap — we demoed flow, answered security, and outlined pilot options. Next steps listed in calendar invite and I'll send materials.

00:49:10 Priya Kapoor: Thanks — one ask: can you share a sample reranker scoring rubric? We grade answers 0,1,2 for relevance.
00:49:22 Liam O'Connor: We'll attach our suggested rubric and a csv template.

00:52:00 Maya Chen: Anything else?
00:52:10 Priya Kapoor: No, just confirm data residency and pilot cost.
00:52:20 Maya Chen: Will do — thanks everyone.
00:52:34 Meeting ended.

Notes:
